references.text: Moses intercedes for the people after they have sinned, appealing to the Lord's honor among the nations, in the same way as in Exodus 32:11
Moses' intercession for Israel where he reminds God that He brought the people out of Egypt with great power and a strong hand
Abraham intercedes for Sodom, an early example of pleading before the Lord's face
Reference to God bringing Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand and great power
The Lord's promise to bring Israel out of Egypt with an outstretched arm and great judgments
The psalm describes how Moses stood in the gap for the people to turn away God's wrath, a direct reference to the incident of the golden calf
Jeremiah intercedes for the people and appeals to God's name and honor
God acted for the sake of His name, so that it would not be profaned among the nations, the same theme as Moses' intercession
The Lord brought Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand and delivered them from the house of slavery
Moses uses identical reasoning (God's deliverance with great power) to turn away God's wrath in two separate crises.
Deuteronomy 9:26 is a direct summary and quotation of Moses' prayer in Exodus 32:11.
Clear contrast: The people use the deliverance as grounds for complaint (17:3), while Moses uses it as grounds for pleading for mercy (32:11).
